newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk helicopter crashes in Iraq, two dead - army.
newsitem.headline: Turk helicopter crashes in Iraq, two dead - army.

text.p: Turkey's military headquarters said on Sunday an army helicopter had crashed in northern Iraq after a "technical fault" during the cross-border operation against separatist Kurdish rebels, killing two pilots.
"A helicopter belonging to the army crashed because of a technical fault on May 18 at 7:30 a.m. (0430 GMT) south of the Cukurca area of Hakkari province," the general staff said in a brief statement.
On Saturday, pro-Kurdish MED-TV said the PKK had shot down a Turkish helicopter near Amediye, 70 km (45 miles) northeast of the Iraqi provincial capital Dohuk. MED-TV offered no other details.
Amediye is just across the Iraqi border from the Turkish province of Hakkari.

Journalists have been barred from the region by Turkish troops and their Iraqi Kurdish allies, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP). Communications were also blocked, making independent confirmation of this and other incidents impossible.
The five-day-old operation against PKK guerrilla bases inside the Kurdish "safe haven" of northern Iraq has drawn criticism from Ankara's Western allies and the United Nations.
The military has said they have killed 902 guerrillas so far for the loss of 12 members of the security forces.

The Germany-based DEM agency, which is close to the PKK, said in a statement on Saturday that more than 40 Turkish soldiers had been killed in clashes with the rebels. It gave no figure for PKK losses.
